speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the leg or foot? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bladder or bowel control, such as incontinence or retention?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me if you feel any weakness when trying to lift your foot or stand on your toes? Also, does coughing or sneezing make the pain significantly worse?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty lifting your big toe or foot upwards, or standing on your heels? I need to assess for specific nerve root involvement, so please let me know if you feel any weakness or numbness in the top of your foot.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sudden onset during exercise and radiation to the foot, I suspect an L5 or S1 radiculopathy, likely from a herniated disc. REQUEST TEST: MRI Lumbar Spine
